notes: Rule 14's correlative clause is read here against two present waws: the earlier waw takes 'both' and the waw between the two coordinated members takes 'and', counting connective morphemes against the ASV's connectives as rule 42 directs. Giving the pair wholly to one waw would leave the other unrendered with an English connective standing exactly at its position.
The first biʿărû takes 'shall make fires' headed on the complement (rule 44) because no ʾēš stands in that clause; the second keeps only 'make' because ʾēš is written.
maqqēl yāḏ → 'handstaves' is rule 30 fusion of a full lexical pair, headed on maqqēl; the four bare bə's the ASV leaves unrendered are unrepresented under rule 40.
